slides.texte_overlay:
How to stay calm when
everyone else is stressed
Breathe slower than the room. When people rush and raise their voices, slow your breathing. Your body calms first, then your words follow.
Focus on the next step, not the whole problem. "What can we do right now?" One clear action calms everyone faster than long discussions.
Lower your voice when tension rises. A calm, low voice makes people stop and listen. Shouting only adds more stress. Calm voices win.
Keep perspective. Ask "will this matter in a year?" Most stressful moments look small once they've passed. Zoom out and breathe before you react.
Before: other people's stress became mine. After: five minutes a day of history, art or science, and I stay steady when things get tense.
slides.texte_sophia: Before: other people's stress became mine. After: I do five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. History, art, science. I stay steady when things get tense.

slides.texte_overlay: Sleep well before big days. Tired men panic faster. A good night's rest is your best preparation for stressful moments. Protect it.
Have a ritual to reset. A walk, a glass of water, two minutes alone. Small breaks help you come back calmer and clearer.
